A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 31-page versions of the same paper. Text and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the main text, algorithms, equations, references, and Appendices A–B.

before.justification: v3 reports theoretical algorithms, sample-complexity and regret bounds, and proofs. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v4 remains a theoretical paper. Inspection of the main text and Appendices A–B establishes that no original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain their procedures, objectives, estimators, and parameter choices, including PAC-COMBAND, its single-label variant, and EXP4-COMB-SPARSE.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical test scenarios. The contextual semi-bandit, list-classification, single-label, and adversarial-regret settings remain the same theoretical settings.

E2.justification: No comparison methods are empirically evaluated in either version. The discussions of EXP4 and previously established learning bounds are retained.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental evaluation protocols. The theoretical sampling procedures, sample requirements, and oracle-call budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies. Appendices A–B retain theoretical algorithms and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical probability guarantees and variance bounds are unchanged.

E6.justification: The reported sample-complexity and regret formulas retain their numerical form, including the K^7 single-label dependence and sm/ε² lower bound. No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: The bounds, hard-instance construction, and mathematical derivations are retained. Theorems 2 and 5 explicitly restate the existing action space of all m-subsets. Appendix A.4 moves the existing Yao argument into the proof; this does not introduce a new extension to randomized algorithms.

C1.justification: v3's abstract claims matching full-information leading rates and essentially cost-free bandit feedback when s=O(1); v4 replaces this with independence of the leading term from K. Section 1.1 also withdraws the assertion that the lower bound establishes optimality of the dominant term. Together these substantially narrow the qualitative PAC claims, although the quantitative guarantees remain unchanged.

C2.justification: A new footnote in Section 1.1 and paragraph in Section 3.2 explain the unresolved log|Π| gap. Because the lower-bound construction has a policy class exponential in m, its m-dependence might come from log|Π|, leaving the additional m factor in the upper bound potentially unnecessary. Other limitations and open problems are retained.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, algorithm parameters, and ERM-oracle access assumptions are unchanged. Neither version adds implementation resources, hardware information, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: The abstract withdraws the general comparison claiming full-information-rate matching, narrowing the contribution's positioning relative to full-feedback learning. The cited works and detailed related-work discussion are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, contribution summary, lower-bound discussion, and theorem wording, plus an added footnote and relocation of the Yao explanation. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote and lower-bound discussion cause limited text and reference reflow; the lower-bound proof sketch now starts on page 11 instead of page 10. The single-column design and algorithm displays are retained, with no figures or tables added.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the accuracy of the paper's message by withdrawing full-information-rate matching and optimality claims that the retained bounds do not establish. Sections 1.1 and 3.2 now explain the unresolved relationship between m and log|Π|. This is a clear improvement in qualification and transparency, while the algorithms, quantitative guarantees, and proofs themselves remain unchanged.
